chapter: Jess Stacy, Goodman and New York characters
title: Marsala's big band at Loew's State and Jess Stacy's refusal
summary: Hodes recalls Joe Marsala's big band at Loew's State and the saxophone section rehearsing a break. He then tells how Jess Stacy turned Goodman's concert offer down.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x:
I got involved in a big band once, through Eddie Condon. It was Joe Marsala's big band, at Loew's Nose as he called it, Loew's State Theatre. And I've seen that big band. And I remember that saxophone section, after every show rehearsing. 29 shows, they rehearsed after every show, trying to get that break right.

It was a 32-bar tune, and at the end of the 29th bar, there was a two-bar break, and one of the saxophone players was supposed to come in. Now, if I may say, there was a beat like this, boop, and then he was supposed to come, boop-bee. He never made it. He never made it on time. And they're back there scuffling Joe Marsala finally made him the band boy after that. He felt sorry for him.

But this was my experience, hearing saxophones, and every note I hit has to correspond with what those seven saxophones are playing, and whether I'm not capable, or whether I just don't care to do it, it's not my bag. So I stayed out of it, and I was glad. It was no disappointment on my part. If it was the Benny Goodman Quartet, it would have been a disappointment. But it was not, it was taking Jess's place.

And the funny thing about Jess, he talked to me recently. Benny wanted him to go to New York for that concert. And he offered him $1800. And Jess says, well, now, let me see, I'm going to be there five days. New York hotels, I won't

travel without my wife, so I got to pay the airfare both ways. I don't have any winter clothes, and it's winter. So I'm going to have to go -- and themore he thought about it, the more the answer came out no. And he told him no, it's not enough money.

But I knew beyond that, it wasn't all the money. He just did not want that experience again. He just had had it. He was delighted with his life. And it was the same Jess that, when he picked up my book and read it, he wrote me a letter that I've still got, just glowing, knocked him out, to find that the story about him was there, just as he had said it.
